questions.stem: In Control Panel, where do you configure a corporate VPN connection or a proxy server?

choices.text: Internet Options, on the Connections tab

questions.explanation: Internet Options' Connections tab is where you configure a VPN or a proxy server in classic Control Panel.
questions.trap: Programs and Features is for installing/removing software, not for network connection settings.

questions.stem: A user accidentally opened a file that turned out to be malicious because Windows was hiding its real .exe extension. In File Explorer Options, which view-tab change prevents this in the future?

choices.text: Uncheck 'Hide extensions for known file types'

questions.explanation: Unchecking 'Hide extensions for known file types' makes Windows display the real extension on every file, exposing things like document.pdf.exe.
questions.trap: Showing hidden files reveals system items but does NOT expose extensions on visible files.

questions.stem: Which Power Options statement is correct?

choices.text: Sleep saves your work to the storage drive and powers the system off completely
Hibernate keeps work in RAM; Sleep saves to the storage drive
Sleep keeps your work in RAM for a quick resume; Hibernate saves to the storage drive and powers off completely
Both Sleep and Hibernate fully power off the system

questions.explanation: Sleep keeps work in RAM (low power, quick resume). Hibernate writes state to the storage drive and powers off (essential before removing the battery).
questions.trap: The reversed claim (Hibernate in RAM, Sleep to disk) is the trap; if RAM loses power, anything held only in RAM during Sleep is lost.

questions.stem: A workstation needs a larger paging file. Where in Control Panel do you configure the virtual-memory paging file?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory settings (the paging file) live under the System applet's Advanced system settings.
questions.trap: Power Options controls hibernation, not the paging file size.

questions.stem: A developer needs to enable Internet Information Services (IIS) on a Windows workstation. Which Control Panel applet exposes this?

choices.text: Programs and Features -> Turn Windows features on or off

questions.explanation: Programs and Features has 'Turn Windows features on or off', which is where built-in components like IIS are enabled.
questions.trap: Internet Options handles browser settings, not Windows components.

questions.stem: In Windows Settings -> Update & Security, what is the purpose of configuring Active Hours?

choices.text: Prevent Windows from rebooting during the user's normal workday

questions.explanation: Active Hours tells Windows when the user is working, so it avoids automatic restarts during that window.
questions.trap: Active Hours does NOT pause updates; it only avoids unexpected reboots during the configured hours.

questions.stem: Why is the system Time and Language setting flagged as critical in a corporate environment?

choices.text: It changes the keyboard layout for international employees only
Correct time is required for encryption and Active Directory to work properly
It controls which Windows Update region is used

questions.explanation: Correct system time is required for encryption and Active Directory authentication to work. Bad time = Kerberos and certificate failures.
questions.trap: Keyboard layout is configured in Region/Language but is not why time itself is critical.

questions.stem: Where in the modern Windows Settings app do you configure sign-in options like a PIN or multi-factor authentication?
questions.explanation: Settings -> Accounts is where you configure Microsoft / local user accounts and sign-in options like a PIN or MFA.
questions.trap: Privacy controls what apps can access (mic, camera) - not the sign-in method.

questions.stem: A laptop user wants closing the lid to write state to the drive and fully power off so the battery can be removed. Which Power Options choice fits?
questions.explanation: Hibernate writes state to the storage drive and powers off completely, which is exactly the condition needed to safely remove the battery.
questions.trap: Sleep keeps state in RAM; removing the battery would lose that work.

questions.stem: In Network and Sharing Center, going into an adapter's properties lets you do what?

choices.text: Configure IPv4 settings - either set IP/DNS manually or use DHCP

questions.explanation: An adapter's properties in Network and Sharing Center is where you set its IPv4 settings (IP, subnet, gateway, DNS) or switch to DHCP.
questions.trap: Firewall rules live under Windows Defender Firewall, not in an adapter's properties.
